server_scripts.name: Drive — Deactivate Document
server_scripts.script:
# Withdraw a document from use. Nothing is deleted.
#
# This replaced a step that trashed the Drive file. A controlled document that
# has been superseded or retired still has to be producible: an auditor asking
# "what did the 2026 policy say, and who withdrew it?" needs the text, not a
# tombstone. So the file, its content and every version snapshot are kept, and
# the document is marked Inactive instead.
#
# The Drive sharing is revoked by the "Revoke Sharing" connector task that runs
# straight after this one — hence revoke=False here. That call lives on the
# diagram rather than in this script so that a reader of the map can see that
# access is withdrawn, and so the scope of the revocation stays configurable
# without a code change.
from one_fm.one_fm.doctype.document_register.document_register import deactivate

reference_document = task_data.get("reference_document")

request = None
if task_data.get("context_doctype") == "Document Request":
	request = task_data.get("context_docname")

if not reference_document:
	frappe.log_error(
		title="Drive Script: deactivate_document — missing reference_document",
		message=f"task_data keys: {list(task_data.keys())}",
	)
else:
	try:
		outcome = deactivate(
			reference_document,
			reason=task_data.get("requirement_text"),
			via_request=request,
			revoke=False,
		)
		result["deactivated_document"] = reference_document
		result["deactivated"] = outcome.get("ok")

		# Downstream needs the file id to revoke sharing on. Publishing it under
		# the same `drive_file` contract the rest of the pipeline uses means the
		# revoke task reads it exactly the way every other Drive task does.
		file_link = frappe.db.get_value("Document Register", reference_document, "drive_file_link")
		result["drive_file"] = {"id": reference_document, "webViewLink": file_link or ""}
	except Exception:
		frappe.log_error(
			title="Drive Script: deactivate_document failed", message=frappe.get_traceback()
		)
		result["deactivated"] = False

server_scripts.name: Drive — Fetch Guideline Content
Drive — Gather Reference
Drive — Index Document
server_scripts.script:
# Register the published document and record this publish as a version.
#
# Runs at publish, after the finalized content has been pushed to Drive. Two
# things happen here, and the order matters: the version record is written from
# the content that was just published, and only then does the register's own
# `content` field move on to it.
#
# Every revision shares one Drive file, so Drive holds only the newest text —
# the moment "Save Final Content to Drive" runs, the previous revision is gone
# from Drive for good. The Document Revision row created below is therefore
# the only surviving copy of what each revision said, which is what makes
# "version 2 changed X" answerable at all.
from one_fm.one_fm.doctype.document_register.document_register import allocate_document_code

drive_file = task_data.get("drive_file") or {}
file_id = drive_file.get("id") or task_data.get("create_file_file_id")
link = drive_file.get("webViewLink") or task_data.get("create_file_file_link") or ""

title = task_data.get("document_title") or task_data.get("title") or "Untitled"
document_type = task_data.get("document_type") or ""

# The snapshot is read back FROM THE DOCUMENT, not from what the AI drafted.
#
# It used to come from task data (`document_markdown`, and `sop_markdown` before
# the Document Request unification renamed it). That was wrong twice over once
# the process started filling a branded template: the author does their final
# corrections in the Drive document, so task data holds the pre-review draft, and
# a document assembled by filling template cells has no markdown to hold in the
# first place. "Read Published Text (Drive)" now supplies it.
#
# The old names are still read as a fallback so an instance that started before
# this change still publishes its content rather than an empty string.
content = (
	(task_data.get("published_content") or {}).get("text")
	or task_data.get("document_markdown")
	or task_data.get("sop_markdown")
	or ""
)
# A Drive text export always starts with a BOM. Left in, it makes an otherwise
# empty snapshot look like content to every truthiness check downstream.
content = content.lstrip("\ufeff")

request = None
if task_data.get("context_doctype") == "Document Request":
	request = task_data.get("context_docname")

if not file_id:
	frappe.log_error(
		title="Drive Script: index_document — no file id",
		message=f"task_data keys: {list(task_data.keys())}",
	)
else:
	try:
		is_existing = frappe.db.exists("Document Register", file_id)
		if is_existing:
			entry = frappe.get_doc("Document Register", file_id)
		else:
			entry = frappe.get_doc({
				"doctype": "Document Register",
				"drive_file_id": file_id,
				"source_process": task_data.get("process_model") or "",
			})

		if not entry.document_code:
			entry.document_code = allocate_document_code(document_type)

		published_version = (entry.current_version or 0) + 1

		# The engine can dispatch one service task twice (the do_engine_steps
		# callback and the STARTED loop both fire on completion). Bumping the
		# version again would invent a revision nobody authored, so a repeat of
		# the same content is recognised and left alone.
		already = frappe.db.get_value(
			"Document Revision",
			{"document": file_id, "version": entry.current_version or 0},
			["name", "content_snapshot"],
			as_dict=True,
		)
		is_repeat = bool(already) and (already.get("content_snapshot") or "") == content
		if is_repeat:
			published_version = entry.current_version or 0

		entry.title = title
		entry.document_type = document_type
		entry.drive_file_link = link
		entry.content = content
		entry.current_version = published_version
		# Publishing is by definition putting a document into use. This matters
		# for a document withdrawn and later revised: the register must not still
		# claim it is out of use once a new revision has been approved.
		entry.lifecycle_state = "Active"
		entry.save()

		if not is_repeat:
			version = frappe.get_doc({
				"doctype": "Document Revision",
				"document": entry.name,
				"document_code": entry.document_code,
				"version": published_version,
				"title_at_version": title,
				"document_type": document_type,
				"drive_file_link": link,
				"content_snapshot": content,
				"published_on": frappe.utils.now_datetime(),
				"published_by": frappe.session.user,
				# The second approval is assigned from approver_user, so that is
				# who signed the content off.
				"approved_by": task_data.get("approver_user"),
				"change_reason": task_data.get("requirement_text"),
				"document_request": request,
			})
			version.insert()
			result["version_record"] = version.name

		result["indexed"] = True
		result["document_code"] = entry.document_code
		result["document_version"] = published_version

		# Stamp the document back onto the request that asked for it, so the
		# requester can open it from the form they raised. Nothing else can do
		# this: "Set Status: Published" is an update_field task using
		# frappe.db.set_value, so no doc hook fires at publish and the request's
		# own app never learns what was created.
		#
		# Written straight to the database because all three fields are read-only
		# and derived — bumping `modified` would hand a stale-document error to
		# anyone with the form open, in exchange for a URL nobody typed.
		if request and frappe.db.exists("Document Request", request):
			frappe.db.set_value(
				"Document Request",
				request,
				{
					"document_link": link,
					"reference_document": entry.name,
					"document_version": published_version,
				},
				update_modified=False,
			)
			result["document_link"] = link
	except Exception:
		frappe.log_error(title="Drive Script: index_document failed", message=frappe.get_traceback())
		result["indexed"] = False

server_scripts.name: Drive — Locate Existing File
server_scripts.script:
reference_document = task_data.get("reference_document")
if not reference_document:
	frappe.log_error(
		title="Drive Script: locate_existing_file — missing reference_document",
		message=f"task_data keys: {list(task_data.keys())}",
	)
else:
	try:
		entry = frappe.get_doc("Document Register", reference_document)
		result["create_file_file_id"] = entry.drive_file_id
		result["create_file_file_link"] = entry.drive_file_link
		# unified contract for downstream connector/script tasks
		result["drive_file"] = {"id": entry.drive_file_id, "webViewLink": entry.drive_file_link}

		# The revision needs to know what it is revising. The drafting task is
		# shown this as *reference only* — it matches the existing structure and
		# tone against it, while the content itself comes from the New Content
		# Document the requester supplied. Without it the AI would be asked to
		# reformat a document it has never seen.
		result["existing_content"] = entry.content or ""
		result["existing_version"] = entry.current_version or 0
		result["existing_document_code"] = entry.document_code or ""
	except Exception:
		frappe.log_error(title="Drive Script: locate_existing_file failed", message=frappe.get_traceback())
